predecessors.name: Khitan Confederation
predecessors.text: the Khitan homeland south of the Xar Moron and east of the Laoha river, under the Yaonian clan until Abaoji's accession

successors.name: Jin dynasty (Jurchen Jin)
successors.text: Manchuria, the Liaoxi and eastern Inner Mongolia, the Liao circuits taken 1115-1125

successors.name: Qara Khitai (Western Liao)
successors.text: the successor state established by Yelu Dashi in the Western Regions, which 'in 1124 officially adopted the dynastic name Great Liao'

capitals.name: Khitan royal camp (ordo) on the Xar Moron

ledger.x: 907: Abaoji becomes khagan of the Khitans.
916: Abaoji takes the title of Celestial Emperor.
918: the first walled capital.
922: the Khitan lands extend west.
926: the Khitans destroy Balhae.
926: the steppe to the Altai edge.
926: the Dongdan kingdom under Yelu Bei.
936: Dongdan is absorbed into the Liao.
28 November 936: the Later Jin is founded as a Liao client.
938: the Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Khitans.
942: Shi Chonggui breaks the subordination.
944: the Liao invade the Hebei plain.
11 January 947: Kaifeng falls to the Liao.
January 947: the Liao annex the Later Jin realm.
947: the dynasty takes the name Great Liao.
947: the Liao lose the Central Plain to the Later Han.
979: the Song attack Youzhou and lose at the Gaoliang River.
983: the name goes back to Great Khitan.
1005: the Chanyuan Treaty.
1010: the Liao invade Goryeo with 400,000 and burn Kaesong.
1014: the Liao take the Poju (Uiju) region.
1022: peace with Goryeo.
1031: the Liao cede territory round the Yalu to Goryeo.
1066: Daozong restores the name Great Liao.
By the 11th century the Jurchens were Liao vassals: 'By the 11th century, the Jurchens had become vassals of the Khitan rulers of the Liao dynasty'.
September 1114: Aguda rebels.
November 1114: the Jurchens win at Chuhedian.
January 1115: the Jurchen confederation becomes the Jin.
January 1115: the war on the Liao continues under the Jin; in August 1115 'his army conquered Huanglong Prefecture'.
August 1115: Huanglong falls to the Jin.
1120: the Supreme Capital falls.
1122: the Central Capital falls.
1122: the Western Capital falls.
1122: the Southern Capital falls.
1124: Yelu Dashi founds the Western Liao.
26 March 1125: the last Liao emperor is taken.
26 March 1125: the Liao end.

wars.name: Khitan conquest of Balhae
wars.outcome: The Khitans besieged Shangjing (Balhae's capital) and forced its surrender in 926; Dongdan was set up under Yelu Bei and its people were relocated in 929.

wars.name: Liao intervention in China
wars.outcome: The Khitans backed Shi Jingtang in 936 (Sixteen Prefectures ceded 938) and the Later Jin emperor surrendered to them in January 947; they withdrew.

wars.name: Song-Liao wars
wars.outcome: Liao wins at the Gaoliang River (979) and in 986; Liao advance toward Kaifeng in 1004; the Chanyuan Treaty of January 1005 fixes the border and the Song pay tribute.

wars.name: Goryeo-Khitan War
wars.outcome: Invasions in 993, 1010 (Kaesong burnt) and 1018-1019 (defeat at Gwiju); peace and Goryeo's adoption of the Liao reign title in the fourth month of 1022; the Liao later ceded land around the Yalu.

wars.name: Liao-Xia wars
wars.outcome: Liao invasions of Western Xia in 1044 and 1048 failed to take the capital; peaceful relations were restored by 1053.

wars.name: Liao campaigns against the Ganzhou Uyghurs and the Zubu
wars.outcome: Expeditions in 1008-1010 against the Ganzhou Uyghurs, a failed siege of Ganzhou in 1027, and the defeat of the Zubu tribes after Mogusi's death in 1100 (about two more years).

wars.name: Jin conquest of the Liao
wars.outcome: The Jin took Ningjiangzhou (1114), Huanglong (1115), the five capitals (1120-1122) and the emperor (early 1125); the Song took Yanjing from the Jin in 1123 and lost it in 1125.

certainty.note: Steppe and tribal frontiers; the Song frontier is also unfixed before Chanyuan.
Only the Song frontier is sharp ('the disputed border would be finalized' in 1005); the steppe, Xia, Jurchen and Goryeo frontiers stay soft.
The Jin conquest, capital by capital.
